top_story.headline: Quiet Saturday: no disclosures or foreign-agent contacts, but a Binance lobbying contract ends
top_story.dek: No new OGE, FARA or House and Senate financial disclosure filings came in, so the day's news sits in the lobbying database.
paragraphs: No filings turned up in the OGE, FARA or House and Senate disclosure searches for this window, and none of the deterministic checks (presidential trades, pardon lobbying, ethics agreements, stopped traders) found anything. The Senate eFD check failed on a parse error, so the Senate side could not be verified.

The most notable lobbying item is the termination of Perspective Strategies's work for Nest Services Limited, the Binance entity, which reported $30,000 in income on digital-asset policy. The filing lists two covered positions: Ryan Taylor, a former Senate HELP Committee deputy communications director, and Stephen Aaron, a former Senate Environment and Public Works Committee research analyst. The registration ended September 30, 2026. Termination filing.

Another notable item: Liberty Government Affairs reported $40,000 in third-quarter income from WuXi AppTec Sales LLC. A separate filing shows TSG Advocates DC, LLC terminated its registration for the same client, filed through Liberty, on October 23.

sections.eyebrow: Contacts With the President, VP & Cabinet
sections.headline: One LDA filing lists the President and Vice President as lobbied; no FARA contacts
paragraphs: No FARA filings were in the top-officials block. One LDA filing names the White House as a lobbying target.

items: Military Officers Association of America (self-filed, third-quarter report): entities lobbied include the Office of the Vice President, the President and the Vice President. Issues include the Love Lives On Act of 2025, the National Defense Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2026, a TRICARE Select pregnancy pilot program, the Health Care Fairness for Military Families Act of 2025 and the HOMEFRONT Act of 2025. Filing.

sections.headline: No new OGE ethics filings to report
paragraphs: No new ethics filings were received during the reporting window. OGE filings include public financial disclosures, ethics agreements, and certification of divestiture documents.

sections.headline: 10 new registrations, 6 terminations and a mostly routine batch of quarterly reports

The table lists every new registration and termination plus the activity reports with notable signals. blocks.text: Largest self-filed spenders this batch: the American Property Casualty Insurance Association reported $1,410,000 in expenses on an amendment (L18) and the Military Officers Association of America $1,070,863 (L19). Other flagged reports include the National Education Association at $670,000 (L20) and the Business Software Alliance at $430,000 (L21). Several filings are repeat reports from the same firm for the same client across quarters, including Furrow Strategies for the American Trade Association for Cannabis and Hemp and The Ferguson Group for the Cape Fear Public Utility Authority. The rest of the 52 flagged and 58 unflagged activity reports are omitted as routine.

sections.headline: No new House or Senate disclosures
